faq.q1: What can I do without an account?
faq.a1: Browse every course, career and roadmap. Reading lessons and tracking progress need an account.

reference.title: Scene reference
reference.camera: position [x, y, z], optional target, fov, controls (orbit or none), autoRotate.
reference.objects: Up to {max}. Each has an id and a shape, and optionally size, position, rotation (degrees), color (#rrggbb), opacity, wireframe, emissive, text (a floating label), info (title and text shown on click) and parent (an id, to move with a group). Shapes:
reference.animation: On an object: type spin, bob, pulse or orbit; axis x, y or z; speed; amount.
reference.links: Up to {max} lines between object ids: color, dashed, label, and flow (count, speed, color) for moving packets.
reference.steps: Up to {max} guided steps: title, text, and show, hide or highlight lists of ids, plus an optional camera. Each step builds on the one before.
reference.lights: Up to {max}: ambient, directional, point or hemisphere, with intensity, color and position. Sensible lighting is added when you list none.

scriptReference.title: Script reference
scriptReference.intro: Your code runs once to build the scene. Available names:

scriptReference.flags: the reader's colour theme, and whether they asked for reduced motion
scriptReference.limits: Up to 20,000 characters. Setup must finish within 3 seconds and frames must keep coming, or the view is shut down. No network access, DOM or timers beyond onFrame.

assessment.title: Knowledge assessment
assessment.metaDescription: Forty questions across eight security domains, scored with a published formula.

intro.honest: This is a fixed questionnaire, not an adaptive or AI test. Everyone answers the same questions, and your score comes from the formula on this page.
intro.noTimeLimit: No time limit. Answers save as you go, so you can stop and come back.

formula.heading: How you're scored
formula.weight: Each question is worth its difficulty: 1 point for beginner, 2 for intermediate and 3 for advanced questions.
formula.unanswered: Unanswered questions count as wrong once you submit.
formula.domain: A domain score is the points you earned divided by the points available in that domain. The overall score uses the same formula across all questions, so it is not an average of the domains.
formula.bands: Below {developing}% is a gap, {developing}% to {developingTop}% is developing, and {strength}% or more is a strength.
